critical.issue: PUT accepts any shape for `hours` (raw dict) but GET returns `List[Location]` with strict Pydantic model where `hours: Dict[str, Dict]`. Writing `hours={'mon': '9-5'}` (string value) succeeds on PUT, then GET /api/locations returns 500 for ALL rows until DB is cleaned. Fix: validate/coerce `hours` on PUT to match schema, or make GET tolerant (drop invalid `hours`). Repro: PUT any location with `{'hours': {'mon': 'anything-not-dict'}}` → then GET /api/locations → 500. Cleaned up DB during test.

context_for_next_testing_agent: Iter 44 shipped /app/backend/routes/finalize.py (large router) + extended settings.py locations + v15 pos tabs. All 22 backend endpoints verified in /app/backend/tests/test_iteration44_finalize.py — reusable regression file. Front-end P0s (Print Routing render, cart no-image, Send-to-Table button+dialog+flow) all confirmed via Playwright on live preview URL. One real bug found: GET /api/locations 500s if hours has any non-dict value written via PUT — high-priority validation gap. Location POST uses LocationCreate which requires 'phone' — my test fixture handled the fallback correctly.
rca of the issue: GET /api/locations pipes raw docs through `Location(**l)`. If any document has `hours` with non-dict value (which PUT does not validate — it just $sets whatever caller sends), pydantic raises ValidationError → 500 for the entire list. Mitigation: (a) add a Pydantic sub-model for hours in the PUT handler, (b) OR wrap Location(**l) in try/except and skip/repair bad rows on read.
